To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a number of medicinal plants used for the treatment of cognitive disorders in Ayurveda and traditional Chinese medicine have the potential to reduce amyloid beta peptide (A beta) production.
plants traditionally used for memory improvement in Ayurvedic medicine and traditional Chinese medicine modulate the expression of amyloid precursor protein and its metabolites in vitro.
the following plants are able to reduce the production of amyloid-beta peptides: Centella asiatica (Linn.) Urb., Ginkgo biloba L. and Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, rapid, and reliable in vitro screening system for the identification of plants with amyloid precursor protein (APP) modulation properties.

the in vitro evaluation of the effect of 10 plant species used in traditional medicine for memory improvement on the modulation of amyloid precursor protein (APP), which is the precursor of the beta-amyloid protein, the principal component in the senile plaque of the Alzheimer brain.
the identification of plants used in traditional medicine for memory improvement that could be used as potential sources of new drugs for Alzheimer disease (AD) treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a lack of scientific evidence to support any of the traditional medicinal uses of these plants for memory improvement.
the plants studied have the potential to be used for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias.

the plant extracts tested in this work, in particular, those of Bacopa monnieri and Centella asiatica, were able to modulate amyloid precursor protein processing in vitro and thus may be useful in the prevention and treatment of AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a number of plants used for memory improvement in Ayurveda and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), that have in vitro amyloid precursor protein (APP) inhibitory activity.

plants used in Ayuvedic and Traditional Chinese Medicine for memory enhancement have a potential to modulate amyloid precursor protein (APP) metabolism, which is the main target in the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease.
plants with the ability to modulate APP and/or Aβ levels in vitro may be useful in the prevention and/or treatment of AD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed and validated a new method to screen for amyloid beta (Aβ) reducing activity in plants.
plants used in traditional Chinese medicine for the improvement of memory may be a source for new anti-amyloid drugs.
the use of traditional medicine for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease should be encouraged.
